name: Slack
summary: Creating and distributing a Slack app is self-serve, but commercial apps need a Marketplace listing (at least 10 active installs, then up to ~11 weeks of review), and unlisted apps are rate-limited on message history.

capabilities.label: Read channel history
capabilities.alternative: Use the Events API to receive new messages instead of polling history.

paths.label: Install in your own workspace
paths.drivenBy: Create the app, add bot and user scopes, register the Composio redirect URI, install to your workspace.
paths.next: Create a Slack app, set redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, add scopes, and create the Composio auth config with its client ID and secret.

untilApproved.text: Use Composio's managed Slack OAuth app for testing; the consent screen shows Composio.

paths.label: Customers' workspaces, unlisted
paths.drivenBy: Activate Public Distribution is self-serve, but Slack's API Terms require a Marketplace listing or a separate agreement to distribute commercially.
paths.costNote: Slack publishes no fee; commercial distribution requires a separate agreement with Slack.
paths.next: Activate public distribution for pilots, and plan the Marketplace listing for commercial launch.

untilApproved.text: Commercial distribution outside the Marketplace needs a separate agreement with Slack.

paths.label: List on the Slack Marketplace
paths.drivenBy: Need 10+ installs on active workspaces held through review, public landing page, privacy policy, support page with 2-business-day response, Security & Compliance section with LLM disclosure, test credentials, optional demo video.
paths.waitOfficial: Up to 10 business days, then up to 10 weeks of functional review
paths.costNote: Slack publishes no submission or listing fee.
paths.next: Get 10 active workspace installs on unlisted distribution, then submit; read-heavy features stay rate-limited until you are listed.

untilApproved.text: Unlisted commercially distributed apps created since 29 May 2025: 1 request per minute and 15 objects per call on conversations.history and conversations.replies.
Submission needs at least 10 active workspace installs (used in the last 28 days), held throughout review.

prereqs.text: Have a Slack workspace you control to create and test the app in.
prereqs.why: The app needs a development workspace. Marketplace submission also requires testing on a second workspace.

prereqs.text: Publish a public landing page made for the Slack app, with a link to a clear privacy policy.
prereqs.why: Every Marketplace app needs both. The landing page cannot sit behind a login or be a PDF, document or code repository.

prereqs.text: Publish a public support page and be ready to answer support requests within 2 business days.
prereqs.why: Slack checks this during Marketplace review.

prereqs.text: Line up at least 10 active workspaces that will install the app before you submit.
prereqs.why: Submissions are blocked below 10 installs on workspaces used in the past 28 days. The count must stay at 10 or more for the whole review.

prereqs.text: Prepare test credentials with dummy data for your service and any third-party service the app connects to. Include a paid account if one is needed.
prereqs.why: Slack asks reviewers to be able to use the full app.

prereqs.text: Decide how you will Commercially Distribute the app: through the Marketplace Agreement or a partner agreement with Slack or Salesforce.
prereqs.why: The API Terms bar Commercial Distribution without a separate agreement.

steps.title: Create the Slack app from a manifest
steps.detail: Generate an app configuration token at api.slack.com/apps (it expires after 12 hours); the agent then creates the app with apps.manifest.create, with the redirect URLs and scopes in the manifest. Tested: created in 0.6 s with no console step.

values.label: Manifest (YAML)
values.text:
display_information:
  name: Your agent
oauth_config:
  redirect_urls:
    - https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add
  scopes:
    bot:
      - chat:write
settings:
  token_rotation_enabled: false

steps.title: Register the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Put Composio's callback in the manifest's redirect_urls. It must match the auth config's redirect URI exactly; Composio's Slack default is …/api/v1/auth-apps/add. The redirect_uri must match, or sit under, a Redirect URL in your settings. HTTPS only, no '#'. Authorization codes expire after 10 minutes.

steps.title: Add only the user scopes your features need
steps.detail: Composio's Slack toolkit connects with user-token scopes (its auth config lists 48 by default), so put yours under user scopes in the manifest and keep the list to what your agent uses. search:read, identity.* and admin.* are common reasons for rejection.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config with your Slack client ID and secret
steps.detail: Create a slack auth config in Composio that uses your own OAuth app credentials and the same scopes you set in step 4. Tested: created through Composio's API in 1.1 s.

steps.title: Install in your own workspace and switch connections to the new auth config
steps.detail: Run the OAuth flow through Composio, approve the scopes, and confirm that the tools work. Then point your agent's connection flow at the new auth config instead of the managed app. Composio's connect link expires about 10 minutes after it is created, so create it when the person is ready to approve. Tested: one approval in Slack, then the connection was active and read-only tool calls worked.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.detail: Manage Distribution → complete the checklist (HTTPS redirect URLs) → Activate Public Distribution. Deactivating later removes the app from other workspaces.

steps.title: Check the connecting user's domain after OAuth for enterprise customers
steps.detail: Slack recommends that apps verify the connecting user's account matches the enterprise customer's expected domain after OAuth. Workspace owners can require approval before members install apps.

steps.title: Reach 10 active workspace installs
steps.detail: Workspaces that used the app in the last 28 days count; sandboxes don't. Keep at least 10 active while the review runs.

steps.title: Draft the Security & Compliance answers, test instructions and demo video script
steps.detail: If the app exposes users to an LLM, disclose the model, data retention and use, tenancy and residency. Slack cannot access any Slack workspace, so give reviewers a way to install the app themselves. A demo video is recommended: show install and OAuth, setup, end-to-end use and uninstall.

steps.title: Submit from the Submit to the Slack Marketplace section of app settings
steps.detail: Submit only once the app is fully functional, publicly installable and tested outside your development workspace. Slack reviews only scopes and features that already exist in the app.

steps.title: Address preliminary review feedback
steps.time: up to 10 business days per round
steps.detail: All feedback must be addressed before the app can be listed. Each resubmission resets your place in the queue.

steps.title: Wait for the functional review
steps.detail: Slack cannot speed up reviews. The estimate on the submission page in app settings may differ from these figures.

steps.title: Publish the approved version when you choose
steps.detail: After publishing, the live version is locked and every update goes back through review. For substantial updates Slack may require a test or staging app identical to the published one.

gotchas.text: Composio's Slack toolkit requests user-token scopes (48 by default), so scopes belong under user scopes in your app. Trim the default list to what your agent uses.

Unlisted commercially distributed apps get 1 request per minute and 15 objects on conversations.history and conversations.replies. Internal and Marketplace apps are exempt; existing installs are not affected.
Slack's API Terms (10 Oct 2025) allow commercial distribution only through the Marketplace or a separate agreement, and ban training large language models on API data.
PKCE is opt-in and permanently turns the app into a public client (30-day refresh tokens, no bot scopes for desktop redirects). Don't enable it for Composio's confidential flow.
Token rotation can't be turned off once on: access tokens then expire every 12 hours and each refresh token works once.
Slack's MCP server has no dynamic registration, and unlisted apps are not allowed to use it.
Workspace owners can require approval before members install apps.

Under the Data Access API and Real-Time Search API terms, you may not keep persistent copies, archives, indexes or long-term stores of other organizations' data. Read literally, this covers persistent vector indexes. Temporary caching is allowed only when essential, and the data must be deleted promptly.

Bulk export of message and file data is not allowed without an additional agreement. Data from one organization may not be used to benefit another. Background collection unrelated to user queries is prohibited.
Free workspaces limit message and file history to 90 days. Apps must not expose data older than that.
Slack may audit your app and act if there is a credible risk of harm. Report unauthorized access to or loss of Slack data promptly to security@slack.com.

blockers.see: Submission blocked on the Marketplace submit page
blockers.cause: Fewer than 10 installs on active workspaces (used in the past 28 days)
blockers.fix: Grow to 10 or more active installs, keep that level through review, then submit.

blockers.cause: Legacy, restricted or broad scopes such as admin.*, identity.*, search:read, workflow.steps:execute or triggers:*, or scopes for features not yet built
blockers.fix: Remove the scopes you do not need, or justify each one with existing functionality, then resubmit.

blockers.see: Preliminary review feedback on the landing page or privacy policy
blockers.cause: Landing page is behind a login, is a PDF, document or repository, or lacks a privacy policy link
blockers.fix: Publish a public web page for the Slack app that links to the privacy policy.

blockers.cause: App is in private beta, still being built, not fully tested, a coded workflow, or trains LLMs on Slack data
blockers.fix: Finish and test the app on another workspace and stop any LLM training on Slack data before you submit.

blockers.cause: You gave test-workspace credentials, but Slack cannot access any Slack workspace
blockers.fix: Give reviewers a way to install the app themselves, plus dummy-data credentials for your service.

blockers.cause: Token request used an unknown client or a code that is not valid
blockers.fix: Check the client ID and secret in the Composio auth config and retry with a fresh code from the authorize redirect.

aiPolicy.summary: Externally offered apps may not use API Data to train LLMs, bulk export messages and files, or use one organization's data to benefit another. Data Access and Real-Time Search API data may not be kept in persistent copies or indexes; temporary caching only, deleted promptly. Marketplace apps exposing users to an LLM must disclose model, retention, tenancy and residency. Apps that train LLMs on Slack data cannot be listed.

customerAdminNote: Workspace owners can require approval before members install apps, and Enterprise Grid orgs require it by default. Ask their admin to approve your app.
unknowns: Whether Composio's managed Slack app is rate-limited as an unlisted app while its Marketplace review is pending.
